newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures slip on firmer yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures slip on firmer yen.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures extended early losses to settle lower across the board on Tuesday, as early bargain-hunting buying lost steam, pressured by the yen's firmer tendency against the dollar, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from 19 yen to 21 yen per gram lower. Most-active benchmark February was off 19 yen at 1,369 yen.
Gold futures opened lower after spot gold tumbled through the $350 an ounce mark overnight in New York.
Spot gold was quoted firmer at $378.00/379.00 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $347.50/348.00 in New York on Monday.

"Benchmark February gold was likely to move within a range of between 1,350 yen and 1,400 yen per gram for a while, sandwiched between bargain-hunting buying and profit-taking," one analyst at a commodity broker said.

Traders said spot gold remained vulnerable to the downside risk with no bullish factors in sight, but added the U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting next week may provide a key for the market.
Platinum and palladium futures also ended lower across the board, but uncertainty over the timing of Russian exports to Japan kept most market players sidelined, traders said.

Despite of the ongoing suspension of Russian exports of platinum group metals to Japan, the tightness in Japan's physical palladium market as eased compared with about one month ago as Japan has boosted metal imports in the spot market, the traders said. Platinum futures ranged from five yen to 17 yen per gram lower, with benchmark February ending down 15 yen at 1,471 yen. Palladium futures ranged from five yen to 14 yen per gram weaker. Benchmark February palladium was off nine yen at 578 yen. Benchmark February silver was down 2.3 yen per 10 grams at 206.8 yen.
